model_labels.char_svm: Char n-gram TF-IDF + calibrated Linear SVM

sanitization_log.note: raw_messages.csv left unchanged on disk (data/raw/); all fixes applied to a copy
missing sender_domain_type -> 'unknown' (kept as its own category)
empty e-mail subject -> '(no subject)'; SMS keeps empty subject by design
'Attachment: file.pdf' lines removed (attachments excluded by SRS)
live-looking http(s):// URLs rewritten to hxxp(s)://host[.]tld (inert strings)
e-mails / phones / card-like numbers / 'password: x' redacted (NFR-02)
URL traits derived from strings only; links never opened (NFR-01)

dedup.method: TF-IDF (1-2 gram) cosine on text with URLs/numbers/names masked; connected components within the same label; keep lowest message_id

leakage_notes: campaign_group perfectly determines the label, so it is excluded from every model input.
sender_domain_type and URL traits are partly informative by construction; the 'text only' ablation shows how much of the result depends on them.
Holdout campaigns are dated later than most training campaigns (time ordering), so a random split would be optimistic.
Near-identical templates were merged BEFORE splitting (FR-01); see dedup_proof.json for the audit.

AT-01.subset: held-out legitimate urgent messages (password-expiry policy + payroll cut-off campaigns)
AT-01.note: Each false alarm costs a helpdesk review and teaches users to ignore warnings; see 'abstain' in the dashboard for how many are routed to human review instead of auto-flagged.

AT-03.limitation: URL traits are parsed only from [.] and (.) defang styles; '[dot]' is not recognised, so link features vanish and the probability shifts. Character substitution and padding also move probabilities because the models rely on exact words.
